0.content: Alice, Klee's mother and a Hexenzirkel mage, met Prune in Nod-Krai when she spotted her reading a pirated travel guide by the road. Prune said the author seemed self-absorbed, with "troubling tendencies" between the lines. Alice then kept ambushing her with absurd questions and debates, rewarding each of Prune's "wins" with prizes. When Descartes had nearly faded away, she cackled like a stage villain, snapped her fingers and announced she had taken him: Prune was now the "Witch Hunter" and must beat every mage, starting with clues from Klee in Mondstadt. Prune screamed after her and set off. In Mondstadt Prune posted notices denouncing the witch "A" as an intellectual bully who abducts "soul companions". Prune calls her a show-off with a hollowed-out hat and the wickedest witch of all.

1.content: Descartes is Prune's imaginary friend: a small dog with indigo and violet markings, a brainy brow and deep dark eyes. He took shape when she, finished with a book too heavy for her age and with no one to talk to, began explaining it to the empty air. She named him after looking for something worthy of "intellectual inquiry". They debate silently ("speech... is far too inefficient") and he points out flaws in her deductions with a glance. In Nasha Town she discussed whether the world is a reflection in a puddle with him, worrying passers-by. He began to fade as Prune grew up too fast; Alice "took" him just before he vanished.

2.content: Prune approached Klee to extract intel on her mother and quickly abandoned an outright abduction plan as beneath a real hunter. Klee instead kept turning up with snacks and toys: crystalfly catching, puddle jumping with Mini Durin, drawing on walls, rolling down Windrise's slopes and long introductions to every Dodoco. "Operation Bake-and-Grill" (cookies for answers) failed completely; Klee's "secret base" was "in the heart". Prune filed one drawing, "Prune and Klee Blow Up Fish Together", in her dossier. The two drew bomb-defusal doodles around Millhaven, then had to scrub the crayon off before being sent to confinement; Klee offered to blow up the wall instead. Klee calls Prune "the best" and plans to take her fish blasting, to Dragonspine and to Simulanka.

3.content: During the limited-time 6.6 flagship event Phantasmal Pals, Prune followed rumours of a witch and a rampaging Forest Boar to Chinju Forest in Inazuma, where she met the Traveler and Paimon and pretended to be Alice's friend. Her bell led them to Klee and the Little Hexenzirkel, a club Klee founded with Yaoyao, Qiqi and Sayu (Paimon joined on the spot). Prune refused to join ("I stopped playing pretend a long time ago") but helped them, and the Yumekui-Baku Hyakujitsuhaku Shion (the "Dough King"), cure the imaginary boar Popcorn. Afterwards she broke down, confessed she was a Witch Hunter, and cried while the little witches held her hands. Persuaded that the Little Hexenzirkel did not exist when Alice set her challenge, she joined, mortified, with the introduction-magic titles "Witch Hunter", "The Only Sane One in a Cruel World (Self-Proclaimed)" and "A Kid Nonetheless". Descartes returned at once.

4.comment: Prune: Witchlure Bell and Hexhunter Oathhammer
4.content: After Descartes was "taken", Prune reviewed every prize Alice had ever given her and picked the two most promising. The bell ("When the bell rings, a witch might appear") was really an old Hexenzirkel tea-party bell; the "might" meant attendance was optional. It never guarantees a witch but never fails to start an adventure; in practice it floats, rings at "localised abnormal magical fluctuations", and once summoned a Whopperflower. The hammer was a sculpting tool Alice meant to give Nicole, who declined it politely ("My hobby is sculpting, not construction and demolition"). Prune renamed both after "very logical and practical" modifications, and Aino gave them a more industrial look.

5.comment: Prune: A Proposition Beyond Refutation (Witch's Homework)
5.content: Prune's permanent Witch's Homework quest (6.6). The Traveler found Alice's taunt in the witch's dictionary; Prune's sarcastic "Look at me, I'm an idiot" was replayed by phonographs all over the plaza, and she smashed several with her hammer. Alice then hosted a debate in a magical copy of the Opera Epiclese, with the Traveler as judge and Paimon in the box seats, on the topic "Klee Is a Bad Kid". Prune argued that conduct is not inherited, that Klee accepts her punishments, that the last fish blasting was Alice's idea, that Klee is cute and kind, and that the real "Bad Kid-ult" was Alice. Alice conceded happily, called it a test of Prune's feelings for Klee, granted a "Witch's Blessing" and vanished again.
